summary: Part one explained what crypto is. This one asks whether you should own any, and how much is too much. Manhar Garegrat works through what actually sets Bitcoin's price, why stablecoins are becoming the useful part of the story, how you would compare Bitcoin with Ethereum or Solana, whether a government can simply ban the thing, and where a 1 to 5 per cent allocation might sit in an otherwise ordinary portfolio. His own framing is to start small rather than treat it as an all-or-nothing bet.

seo.title: Can India Really Ban Crypto? Regulation, Stablecoins & What Investors Should Know | Part 2
seo.description: Can India ban crypto? What drives Bitcoin's price, why stablecoins matter, and the 1 to 5 per cent allocation question, with Manhar Garegrat.

takeaways.text: The allocation discussed is 1 to 5 per cent, and the reasoning is to start small rather than make it an all-or-nothing bet. That is a view from the conversation, not a recommendation for your portfolio.
Banning crypto outright is harder than it sounds, and India's position today is better described as a set of separate interventions than as one framework.
Stablecoins are where the practical use is showing up first, alongside CBDCs, and they behave very differently from Bitcoin.
Comparing blockchains means understanding the trilemma: security, speed and decentralisation, and which one each network chose to give up.
Custody is the part retail investors skip. Who holds the keys decides what you own when something goes wrong.

fork.decision: Should crypto get a place in an ordinary portfolio?

points.text: The case made is for 1 to 5 per cent, small enough that being wrong does not change your life.
Institutional money, Bitcoin ETFs and real custody infrastructure have arrived since the last cycle.
Stablecoins and tokenised payments are a genuine use, not only a trade.
The technological, regulatory and market risks discussed are real and not yet priced by anyone with confidence.
India has interventions rather than a framework, so the rules you buy under may not be the rules you sell under.
Tax treatment is unforgiving: gains carry TDS and losses cannot be offset.

fork.pick: If you want exposure, take it in a size that cannot hurt you, which is what the 1 to 5 per cent framing is really saying, and sort out custody before you sort out which coin. If that sounds like too much work for a sliver of your portfolio, owning none is an entirely respectable answer.
